records.title: Managerial Economics
records.text: B ECON 300 Managerial Economics (4) Analysis of economic factors affecting decisions made by business firms. Demand and cost analysis, and alternative policies from the firm's point of view. Prerequisite: ACCTG 225; ECON 201; either MATH 112, MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 127, MATH 134, or Q SCI 291; either IND E 315, QMETH 201, Q SCI 381, PSYCH 315, PSYCH 318, STAT 220, STAT 221/SOC 221/CS&SS 221, STAT 311, or STAT 390; may not be repeated.

records.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
records.text: B ECON 301 Intermediate Macroeconomics (4) Analysis of economy with attention to the business cycle, output of goods and services (GNP), inflation, unemployment, and government's fiscal and monetary policies. How the economy affects individuals and firms and how to deal effectively with the economic environment. Prerequisite: ECON 201; may not be repeated.
restrictionPhrases: Prerequisite: ECON 201; may not be repeated.

records.title: Financial Markets
records.text: B ECON 420 Financial Markets (4) Analysis of the structure and functions of the money and capital markets; the saving-investment process and financial intermediaries; supply and demand for lendable funds and the level and structure of interest rates, role of Federal Reserve and Treasury in money market developments. May not be repeated. Prerequisite: B ECON 300 or ECON 300. Offered: jointly with FIN 420.

records.title: Strategy and Economics for Global Business
records.header: B ECON 426 Strategy and Economics for Global Business (4)
records.text: B ECON 426 Strategy and Economics for Global Business (4) Applies strategic and economic frameworks to global business decisions. Topics include global macroeconomics, geopolitics, and trade; cross-border organization and value-chain design; market entry; and platform strategy. Prerequisite: B ECON 300 or ECON 300. Offered: jointly with FIN 426.

records.title: International Finance
records.text: B ECON 427 International Finance (4) Asset choice and institutional operations in international finance, foreign exchange problems, the impact of international financial problems and operations on business, short- and long-term international financing. Course overlaps with: T FIN 440. Prerequisite: either B ECON 300 or ECON 300; may not be repeated.
